dimensions.assessment: Directly affects all persons, businesses, financial institutions, and employers engaging in cash transactions or cash wage payments within the United States.
dimensions.evidence: Any person, including a financial institution, selling goods or services in a cash transaction or entering into any other transaction that results in a payment or transfer of cash

dimensions.assessment: Changes everyday cash transactions by permitting rounding to the nearest five cents and ceases the minting of new pennies for circulation.
dimensions.evidence: Secretary shall cease production of one-cent coins for general circulation, but may continue to produce and issue one-cent coins for sale as numismatic items.

dimensions.assessment: Modifies coin production costs by altering the composition of 5-cent coins and stopping penny production, but specific net fiscal impact numbers are not stated.
dimensions.evidence: reduces the cost incurred to produce such coin

dimensions.assessment: Amends Title 31 of the United States Code regarding coin specifications, creates new cash rounding rules, and overrides conflicting state and local laws regarding rounding.
dimensions.evidence: Any person... shall not be in violation of any Federal requirement, law, regulation, or standard based on the adherence to the cash rounding provisions

dimensions.assessment: Permanent change to U.S. coinage production and cash transaction standards, with initial multi-year reporting requirements.
dimensions.evidence: Notwithstanding any other provision of law, the Secretary shall cease production of one-cent coins for general circulation

importance_detail.rationale: The bill stops the production of the penny for general circulation, permits cash transactions and cash wages to be rounded to the nearest five cents, and mandates Federal Reserve reporting on coin terminal operations and distribution stability.

summary: The Common Cents Act directs the U.S. government to stop producing one-cent coins for general circulation, permits voluntary rounding to the nearest five cents for cash transactions, and changes the material composition of five-cent coins to reduce production costs. Existing pennies remain legal tender, and non-cash payment methods are unaffected.

affected_groups.effect: Individuals and businesses engaging in cash transactions may voluntarily round totals or change to the nearest five cents when exact change is unavailable.
Workers receiving cash wages whose pay is not divisible by five cents will have their pay rounded up to the nearest five cents if their employer chooses to round.
Stops general circulation production of the penny and is authorized to alter the metal composition of the five-cent coin.

key_provisions: The Department of the Treasury must stop producing the one-cent coin for general circulation, though production for collectors may continue.
Previously minted pennies retain their status as legal tender.
The Secretary of the Treasury may alter the composition of the five-cent coin using zinc and nickel layers to lower production costs.
Parties in a cash transaction may voluntarily round totals or change ending in 1, 2, 6, or 7 down, and 3, 4, 8, or 9 up to the nearest five cents.
Employers paying wages in cash who choose to round must round the amount up to the nearest five cents.
Cash rounding rules do not apply to checks, electronic fund transfers, credit cards, or other non-cash payment methods.
The Federal Reserve must submit a strategic plan and multiple progress reports regarding coin terminal operations and distribution stability.
missing_information: Exact dates for when the Treasury will cease penny production, other than taking effect one year after the date of enactment.
Specific details on the exact cost savings expected from changing the five-cent coin composition.
summary_detail.plain_summary: The Common Cents Act directs the U.S. government to stop producing one-cent coins for general circulation, permits voluntary rounding to the nearest five cents for cash transactions, and changes the material composition of five-cent coins to reduce production costs. Existing pennies remain legal tender, and non-cash payment methods are unaffected.
summary_detail.significance: This bill alters the U.S. coinage system by ending production of the penny and permitting nationwide cash transaction rounding. The impact covers anyone using physical cash for purchases, sales, or wage payments, as well as federal coin production operations.
